01 · A creative change of method

Combine first.
Discover what it means.

“An odd combination of different cultural forms that feels familiar but combined in a totally different way.”

The earlier atlases remain the process record. This lab opens the material again: antiquity, court dress, wraps, tailoring, contemporary fashion and Olympic athletic silhouettes can all meet in the same garment.

What changes in this pass

Sharp finish, controlled volume, tension, precise edges and stronger colour take the lead. Exposed skin can be elegant, ceremonial, forceful, playful or athletic. Repair and bagginess no longer supply the default visual identity.

The forms are allowed to exceed present-day expectations of ordinary clothing. A convincing alternative world can develop its own visual confidence and formalities.

What makes a collision meaningful

Change where a garment carries weight, how it frames the body, which direction it reads, or what it exposes. Let the combination alter construction and proportion rather than simply add an emblem.

School assignment comes after this exploratory pass. A new silhouette may reveal a useful idea that the earlier school briefs did not anticipate.

Reflect

Mirror.

Duplicate an oblique fold until two directions produce balance.

Displace

Move.

Shift a closure, sleeve or volume away from its expected axis.

Tension

Bind.

Use compact folds and clear limb lines to make force visible.

Recut

Invert.

Keep a familiar outline while changing its coverage, scale or material.

16 experiments across four plates. The drape plate is ceremonial; the suit plate moves from formal to open everyday wear; the last two plates explore fictional athletic dress through modern sport vocabularies.

Plate 01 · Mirror

Mirror the drape.

A familiar diagonal becomes a bilateral architecture.

A1 · The Double PalluA2 · The Inverted CourtA3 · The Twin ObliqueA4 · The Radial Mantle

What emerged / next mutation
The doubled diagonal and radial mantle make the symmetry especially clear. The court look discovers a repeated shoulder-and-hip fan: it reads as an entire bilateral architecture. A next mutation could shrink one of those fans into an athletic waist or expand the mirrored drape into headwear.

A1 · Mirror

The Double Pallu

Forms meeting
Sari-like shoulder drape + narrow tailored column
Operation
Duplicate and reflect the diagonal across the body.
Resulting silhouette
Two equal drapes cross at the sternum and fall as paired back planes.
Material proposition
Cobalt silk, white base, pressed central pleats.

A single directional gesture becomes a shared centre; the body can look both doubled and composed.

A2 · Mirror

The Inverted Court

Forms meeting
Lateral court volume + slim formal underlayer
Operation
Move volume to paired sculpted hip planes.
Resulting silhouette
Equal folded wings counterpoint a narrow upright body.
Material proposition
Ivory, citron inner edge, graphite joins.

Ceremony occupies space through a constructed outline rather than surface wealth.

A3 · Mirror

The Twin Oblique

Forms meeting
Crossed wrap front + tailored split panels
Operation
Repeat an oblique closure until it becomes balanced.
Resulting silhouette
Two crossing fronts and two lower planes make deliberate bilateral tension.
Material proposition
Vermilion, black, sharply pressed folds.

The joining act becomes visible twice; symmetry emerges from two individually asymmetrical actions.

A4 · Mirror

The Radial Mantle

Forms meeting
Accordion pleat + fitted formal column
Operation
Reflect two semicircular fans around the sternum.
Resulting silhouette
Equal pleated shoulders frame the neck and arms with air.
Material proposition
Graphite column, porcelain white fan.

The figure becomes a centre of expansion. Head, shoulder and public space belong to one outline.

Plate 02 · Displace

Break the suit.

Displace the whole architecture, rather than decorate one lapel.

B1 · The Rotated AxisB2 · The Migrating SleeveB3 · The Open Half-FrameB4 · The Collar That Descends

What emerged / next mutation
The spiral sleeve and the glove paired with unequal leg lengths create strong changes of axis. The descending-collar look produces floating collar tongues and hip folds rather than one uninterrupted collar-to-waist construction. That separation could itself become an idea, or the next pass could reconnect them into a continuous line.

B1 · Displace

The Rotated Axis

Forms meeting
Tailored suit + off-axis sculptural plane
Operation
Move the closure, shoulder height and hem to a new axis.
Resulting silhouette
One high shoulder, one short jacket half, one curved long panel.
Material proposition
Graphite, ivory, clean angular shoes.

The inherited image of authority remains recognisable while its centre of gravity moves.

B2 · Displace

The Migrating Sleeve

Forms meeting
Conventional sleeve + spiral wrap construction
Operation
Let a sleeve originate from the waist-to-shoulder fold.
Resulting silhouette
One quiet arm and one arm grown from the turning front.
Material proposition
Emerald, ivory, continuous curved join.

The garment suggests that structure can be generated through motion rather than assembled around a fixed front.

B3 · Displace

The Open Half-Frame

Forms meeting
Cropped tailoring + unequal breeches/trouser legs
Operation
Interrupt the jacket and lower lengths on different sides.
Resulting silhouette
Bare torso, one shoulder frame, one long leg, one knee-length leg, one long glove.
Material proposition
Black, ivory, crisp edges.

Exposure and enclosure alternate around the body; the eye has to travel rather than settle at the centre.

B4 · Displace

The Collar That Descends

Forms meeting
Lapel/collar language + compact folded hip architecture
Operation
Continue the collar through negative space into the waist.
Resulting silhouette
Open chest held between descending bands and compact paired hip fins.
Material proposition
Ivory, black, vermilion ankle boots.

An absent shirt can still have a tailoring logic. The void becomes a designed part of the garment.

Plate 03 · Tension

The athletic knot.

Compact wrapped cloth meets gloves, grips, guards and shoes.

C1 · The Duelling LineC2 · The PugilistC3 · The Ultramarine GymnastC4 · The Ivory Archer

What emerged / next mutation
The compact wraps, clear legs and emphatic hands and feet produce a much sharper sporting language than the earlier loose shorts. The gauntlet and forearm guard emerge as hard moulded shapes. A useful next collision would retain their proportions but translate one into soft stretch fabric, or mirror one glove while shifting the waist in the opposite direction.

C1 · Tension

The Duelling Line

Forms meeting
Fundoshi-like hip folding + fencing gauntlet and leg line
Operation
Anchor the cloth in one dominant diagonal.
Resulting silhouette
Open torso, compact hip wrap, one long glove, fitted socks and low shoes.
Material proposition
White, cobalt, silver.

The waist and the active hand answer one another. Direction is visible before movement begins.

C2 · Tension

The Pugilist

Forms meeting
Broad folded waist + boxing glove and boot volumes
Operation
Compress the lower silhouette and enlarge the extremities.
Resulting silhouette
Bare chest, short taut lower form, sculpted gloves and high laced footwear.
Material proposition
Vermilion, black, controlled satin sheen.

Mass moves away from a loose trunk and toward hands and feet; the athlete reads as compact force.

C3 · Tension

The Ultramarine Gymnast

Forms meeting
Mirrored hip bands + wrist and palm-grip forms
Operation
Build bilateral tension with a very small central fold.
Resulting silhouette
Long clear leg lines, bare feet and equal white wrist structures.
Material proposition
Ultramarine, white, matte stretch.

Grip and release become the compositional contrast: held hands and waist, open torso and feet.

C4 · Tension

The Ivory Archer

Forms meeting
Off-axis hip wrap + forearm guard and split-toe shoe
Operation
Continue a diagonal from the arm into the opposite thigh.
Resulting silhouette
One close curved thigh panel, one more exposed side, one guarded forearm.
Material proposition
Ivory, acid green, refined matte surfaces.

A cross-body line unites reach and stance. The equipment is a proportioning device as well as a borrowed vocabulary.

Plate 04 · Recut

The Olympic body, recut.

Close-fit contemporary sport supplies a second skin to transform.

D1 · The Pleated SprinterD2 · The Mirrored CurrentD3 · The Diagonal VelocityD4 · The Folded Rower

What emerged / next mutation
The hip pleats are compressed directly into the cycling line, while diagonal arm-and-leg coverage gives the racing figure an unbroken direction. The swimmer bands read more like integrated surface panels than a separate folded cloth: deepen them if a more tactile wrap is wanted. The final rowing silhouette turns the waist into an organised crossing without adding loose volume.

D1 · Recut

The Pleated Sprinter

Forms meeting
Cycling race line + compressed divided-pleat geometry
Operation
Miniaturise a broad pleated form into the hip seam.
Resulting silhouette
Sleeveless racing line, fitted lower body, two precise pleated fins, smooth head profile.
Material proposition
Cobalt, white, engineered stretch.

A textile memory survives at a new scale: expansive pleating becomes a compact articulation.

D2 · Recut

The Mirrored Current

Forms meeting
Swimming-jammer column + paired wrap bands
Operation
Make two moving bands converge symmetrically.
Resulting silhouette
Open torso, dark close leg columns and equal white routes around the waist.
Material proposition
Black, white, clean seam lines.

The body reads as flow gathered into one axis.

D3 · Recut

The Diagonal Velocity

Forms meeting
Racing second skin + one continuous wrap axis
Operation
Oppose one long sleeve with the opposite long leg.
Resulting silhouette
A small side opening and unequal arm/leg coverage create counterbalance.
Material proposition
Vermilion, graphite, smooth stretch.

The body carries a direction through its whole length; asymmetry is organised rather than scattered.

D4 · Recut

The Folded Rower

Forms meeting
Rowing/gymnastics singlet + paired waist drapery
Operation
Integrate mirrored crossing bands into a close sporting one-piece.
Resulting silhouette
An athletic torso line flows into a precise crossed waist and compact divided lower form.
Material proposition
Plum, ivory, white wrist cuffs.

A formal wrapping gesture is compressed into athletic construction. The waist carries movement without loose volume.

06 · The selection is another creative act

Choose a collision.
Then mutate it again.

The look descriptions preserve the intended experiments. Images may discover something else. Keep the parts that make a new relationship and mark where to exaggerate, simplify or cross two looks.

Three ways to take a selected look further

Next moveExampleWhat changes
Change scaleTurn a small hip pleat into a shoulder canopy, or compress a broad mantle into a glove cuff.A recognisable construction acquires a new relationship to the body.
Change symmetryMirror a single glove line; then offset the hem to prevent the whole figure from settling.Balance and direction can coexist instead of being opposites.
Change occasionGive an athletic wrap a formal fabric and repeated fold; give a ceremonial drape a close-fit sport base.The form gains another social life without merely adding decoration.
07 · Real sport, freely recombined

A sharper athletic vocabulary.

Research included Olympic fencing, men’s gymnastics, track cycling, boxing and swimming imagery. The references supply gloves, close-fit body lines, waist boundaries, grips, guards and footwear. The combinations here belong to fictional athletic worlds rather than depicting those sports’ actual uniforms.

Fencing: gauntlet, breeches, fitted leg line ↗

Equipment vocabulary and limb proportions. The invented bare-torso ensembles are new combinations.

Boxing: waist, gloves and footwear ↗

A strong waist boundary and distinct hand/foot volumes provide a useful silhouette comparison.

Gymnastics: apparatus and grip vocabulary ↗

The visual research included men on rings and bars, close garment lines, wrist support and palm contact.

Track cycling: one-piece second skin ↗

Smithsonian collection record for Sarah Hammer’s short-sleeved racing skinsuit; also compared with Olympic race photography.

Swimming: jammer and seam architecture ↗

Manufacturer imagery and descriptions provide close-fit lower-body and bonded-seam vocabulary.

Archery: forearm and hand relationship ↗

Federation introduction to equipment supplies the arm-guard reference; the combined outfit is invented.

Visual research accessed 25 October 2026. No reference photograph is reproduced in these plates; all fashion images were newly generated for this lab.

08 · Process record

The earlier atlas
remains the earlier atlas.

The seven-school character register records the previous direction. This volume opens a new combinatory phase in response to Lin Wei’s clarification: imagination and meaningful transformations now lead the design process.

The 16 look registers describe intended construction and expressive possibilities. The “what emerged” notes describe the generated images. School assignments, final garments and later story roles remain available to discover through further combination.

The four images were made using the built-in image-generation tool, without the earlier costume sheets as image references. Original PNGs, same-dimension JPEG copies, exact prompts and the design register are included in the package.
